title: Unable to query duckdb file on S3
body:
### What happens?

When I try to attach to a DuckDB file on S3, I receive the following error:

```
Catalog Error: Cannot open database "s3://bucket/path/to/test.duckdb" in read-only mode: database does not exist
```

Related issue: https://github.com/duckdb/dbt-duckdb/issues/249

Nightly I used: https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/actions/runs/7648092822/artifacts/1193564377 from https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/actions/runs/7648092822

### To Reproduce

1. Create a new DuckDB database called `test.duckdb`.
2. Upload into S3 bucket
3. Set vars and install/load extensions:
```
INSTALL httpfs;
LOAD httpfs;

SET s3_region = 'us-east-1';
SET s3_access_key_id = 's3_access_key_id';
SET s3_secret_access_key = 's3_secret_access_key'; 
```
4. Try to attach to database:
```
attach 's3://bucket/path/to/test.duckdb' as test (READ_ONLY)
```

You should receive an error such as:

```
Catalog Error: Cannot open database "s3://bucket/path/to/test.duckdb" in read-only mode: database does not exist
```

### OS:

macOS 14.2.1  M1 aarch64

### DuckDB Version:

DuckDB v0.9.3-dev3121

### DuckDB Client:

Nightly JDBC, used via DBeaver

### Full Name:

Nat Elkins

### Affiliation:

Knoetic

### Have you tried this on the latest `main` branch?

I have tested with a release build (and could not test with a main build)

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [x] Yes, I have

comments.body:
Okay I can indeed reproduce this issue, the workaround for me is to switch from the `load_aws_credentials()` to the [recommended](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/s3api#config-provider) way of using secrets. 

So for example:

```SQL
CREATE SECRET (TYPE s3, provider credential_chain);
attach 's3://test-bucket-ceiveran/test_attach_issue/test.db' as test (readonly);
```

I see the `aws` extension docs are outdated and still advocate using the `load_aws_credentials()` function
